title: WPSS/1964/2014 of Smt Laleeta Rani Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1964 of 2014
Smt. Laleeta Rani Ö Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents

Mr. Tapan Singh, Advocate, present for the petitioner.
Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.(Oral)
1. The petitioner was a candidate for the selection of
Assistant Teacher in Government Primary School in the year
2011-2012. She had appeared in the said selection process as
an Other Backward Class (hereinafter referred to as ìO.B.C.î)
candidate. For appointment as a teacher in elementary school
qualifying Teachers Eligibility Test (in short ìTETî) or Central
Teacher Eligibility Test (in short ìCTETî) is essential, where 50
percent marks is the requirement qualification for the O.B.C.
candidates. Admittedly the petitioner is an ìOBCî candidate
and she has 51.79 percent marks in the CTET examination.
2. All the same, by order dated 05.11.2014 the
candidature of the petitioner has been rejected by the Director,
Primary Education, Dehradun placing reliance on the decision
of this Court passed in Special Appeal No. 360 of 2012 in
Triveni Chandra Pandey Vs State of Uttarakhand (decided on
26.11.2013). The reliance on Triveni Chandra Pandey is
absolutely misconceived. Though this Court in Triveni Chandra
Pandey has held that making ìresidenceî in a particular district
a mandatory criteria for appointment in public service is in
violation of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
However, since by that time the appointments had already been
made and the selected candidates were already appointed and
were working, this Court had directed not to disturb their
candidatures and had categorically held that this decision will
only take its effect prospectively i.e. for future appointments
only.

3. The candidature of the petitioner is also of the same
selection process, therefore, the decision of this Court passed in
Triveni Chandra Pandey (referred above), is not applicable in the
case of the present petitioner and on that ground the claim of
the petitioner cannot be rejected. It is a wrong interpretation of
the order and learned counsel for the respondents fairly
submitted that it is wrong interpretation by Director Primary
Education, Dehradun.
4. Consequently, the writ petition is disposed of with a
direction to the respondents to consider the case of the
petitioner and give her appointment as an Assistant Teacher,
Government Primary School, in case there is no other
ineligibility attached to her candidature.
5. Let the needful be done as expeditiously as possible,
but definitely within a period of four weeks from the date of
production of certified copy of this order.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
01.12.2014
Nitesh
